headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:2.3}} on the summit of Smugglers' Notch early Monday to Monday afternoon. None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon.
Light rain showers are possible this afternoon and evening, then widespread rain is expected Thursday into Friday.
Some beneficial rain remains likely over the weekend, although chances for heavier amounts have trended downward.

ALY.excerpt:
) Above normal temperatures and mainly dry weather expected through Wednesday.
) A cold front will bring chances for some beneficial showers Thursday, followed by additional chances for rain Friday into the weekend.

GYX.excerpt:
A front will bring chances for showers from the foothills northward today through tonight. Otherwise conditions remain mostly dry through Wednesday with above normal temperatures.
A slow moving cold front and waves of low pressure will bring chances for rain Thursday into the weekend.

BUF.excerpt:
) Unusually warm weather is expected Today and Wednesday, with forecast temperatures potentially reaching record highs for early November.
) High probability for widespread showers Wednesday night through Thursday due to the passage of a cold front. Unsettled weather is expected to continue into the weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
Potential fog development this morning and again overnight tonight, but otherwise, generally tranquil weather prevails through the middle of the week.
The next chance for rain returns late this week and into the weekend.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2-week dry spell coming to an end
) Trending cooler this weekend with showers downwind of Lake Erie

RLX.excerpt:
) A cold front brings showers and possible thunderstorms for Wednesday into Thursday.
) Cool temperatures this weekend, with upper level disturbances providing chances of showers at times.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Some snow early Monday, best at Smugglers' Notch.
paras: Light snow early Monday to Monday afternoon: Smugglers' Notch {{s:2.3}}, Stowe {{s:2.3}}, Jay Peak {{s:1.1}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0,3.9}} at Smugglers' Notch. It's a northwest upslope setup, one that usually favors Smugglers' Notch, Stowe and Jay Peak.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:43}} to {{t:63}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Tuesday 11:57 AM: "Warm temperatures continue through Wednesday with potential for exceeding a few daily records Wednesday afternoon."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:1.1}} at the summit early Monday to Monday morning (models {{r:0,2.4}}). Highs stay near {{t:31}} afterward, so some of it should stick up high.
Too mild to make snow this week: mid-mountain doesn't stay at or below {{t:26}} (counting humidity) for long.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 24 days out.
